title: Task × time-step Mirror normalization View
hypothesis: For four task-specific temporal encodings of MNIST, a shared SNN with one learned temporal-gain profile and one scalar cyclic phase code per task will retain held-out accuracy within 1.5 percentage points of native task×time TEBN while using at least 2% fewer actual serialized inference bytes (<=0.98x native task×time TEBN), and exceed a byte-near rank-1 task×time factor control by at least 1 percentage point.

mirror_insertion.physical_object: one shared input and recurrent synaptic SNN across tasks
mirror_insertion.coordinate: one continuous cyclic phase m per task, shifting the shared learned T×H temporal normalization-gain profile by periodic linear interpolation
mirror_insertion.logical_function: task-specific temporal gain trajectories on shared synapses
mirror_insertion.native_before_m: one shared LIF network with native TEBN gains for each task and time step
mirror_insertion.simple_control: one learned scalar task gain added to the shared T×H log-gain profile (rank-1 task modulation), with exactly the same number of adaptive normalization parameters as Mirror

dataset.name: MNIST
dataset.source: official Yann LeCun IDX gzip files; URLs in source/acquire_mnist.py
dataset.audit_split: official test IDX files, unopened until both development gates pass
dataset.audit_access: gated; no test IDX acquisition/decode before development decision

task_transform.input_encoding: For pixel intensity x∈[0,1], sample Bernoulli spikes with p=min(0.9,0.65*x*envelope[(t-offset) mod 8]); labels are unchanged MNIST digit classes. Equal cyclic shifts preserve total expected spike count.

model.type: single-hidden-layer leaky integrate-and-fire SNN with fast-sigmoid surrogate gradient
model.reset: subtract detached threshold after a spike
model.normalization: positive multiplicative hidden-current gain; no task-specific synapses

training.checkpoint_rule: best development accuracy among fixed checkpoints every 100 updates; ties choose lower dev loss

development_eval.selection: highest aggregate accuracy; tie-break by lower loss

gates.quality_storage: In each development seed, Mirror accuracy must be no more than 1.5 percentage points below native task×time TEBN and actual serialized inference payload must be <=0.98x native TEBN (at least 2% end-to-end byte reduction).
gates.mirror_specific: in each development seed, Mirror accuracy must exceed the byte-near rank-1 task-scalar gain control by >=1.0 percentage point; otherwise no Mirror-specific value is established.
gates.audit: Open official MNIST test files only if both development gates pass in both seeds; apply identical accuracy gates and no tuning.

paid_objects: all shared synaptic and membrane-related learned tensors
all TEBN gains or Mirror temporal profile and phase codes

compute.energy: No hardware energy claim; CPU operation proxy only.

boundaries: Synthetic temporal modulation of MNIST, not a neuromorphic sensor benchmark.
Fixed-budget screen is learning-efficiency/mechanism evidence, not capacity evidence.
Task IDs are known to task-conditioned variants and their code/index overhead is charged.
No hardware-energy or specialized neuromorphic-runtime claim.
Classification has identical label mapping across tasks; this isolates temporal normalization sharing.

amendments.timing: before implementation and any MNIST access
amendments.change: Relaxed end-to-end payload ratio from 0.75x to 0.98x native task×time TEBN.
amendments.rationale: Shape-only parameter accounting before data shows shared synaptic weights contribute ~407 KB, native task×time gains ~16 KB, and Mirror temporal profile+phase coordinates ~4.1 KB, so full payload reduction is only about 3%; a 25% reduction gate would be unattainable even if every Mirror normalization byte were free.

amendments.timing: before implementation and any MNIST access
amendments.change: Aligned the falsifiable hypothesis sentence with the amended 0.98x complete-payload gate.
amendments.rationale: Keep the protocol summary and exact decision gate numerically consistent.

amendments.timing: before implementation completion and before any MNIST access
amendments.change: Made the ordinary gain control an equal-size rank-1 task-scalar modulation of the shared temporal TEBN profile, rather than a learned task×time basis tensor.
amendments.rationale: The initial low-rank control implementation carried an additional free T×H basis and was twice the Mirror adaptation-state size. A task scalar added to the shared profile isolates a simple equal-byte native gate and avoids an unfair parameter budget.

amendments.timing: before implementation completion and before any MNIST access
amendments.change: Fixed development evaluation to a deterministic 2,048-row subset per world across all four tasks, evaluated every 100 updates; audit uses the same row count from official test data with separate locked seeds.
amendments.rationale: Specify compute-bounded fixed evaluation draws and exact paired event-generation seeds before acquiring MNIST.
